instruction: In Chrome, bring up the Google Scholar page for the main corresponding author of this paper.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

metadata.explanation: Paraphrase using 'bring up' and 'main corresponding author'. The PDF footer clearly states 'Correspondence to: Tianlin (Tim) Shi <tianlin@cs.stanford.edu>', identifying him as the main corresponding author. Task requires: (1) reading the PDF to find the corresponding author, (2) searching for 'Tianlin Shi' or 'Tim Shi' on Google Scholar, (3) opening his citations profile (user ID: qRAQ5BsAAAAJ). Evaluator uses existing is_expected_url_pattern_match metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts active Chrome tab URL from accessibility tree, which is the right state to verify task completion
Metric uses appropriate pattern matching logic - checks for both 'https://scholar.google.com/citations' (base URL) and 'user=qRAQ5BsAAAAJ' (specific user ID)
Expected values are semantically correct - user ID qRAQ5BsAAAAJ uniquely identifies Tianlin (Tim) Shi's Google Scholar profile
Complete coverage - if both patterns match in URL, task was definitely completed correctly (user navigated to correct Scholar profile)
Logic will work correctly at runtime - re.search() checks for pattern presence in URL string, no complex parsing needed
No UI state dependencies - URL is read from accessibility tree after navigation completes, not from transient dialogs
